Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in governmental affairs which are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can self-regulate and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of diminishing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, and obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in suffering or misery physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in physical, sexual, and psychological suffering or misery to women, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of persons not to experience discrimination, suffering or misery either directly or indirectly committed by state officials or by the state or by regional government officials or individuals which constitute natural rights granted by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which includes complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT Article 25

Obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:

a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women conducted by the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 8

The implementation of women's protection includes efforts to: a. prevent violence, exploitation, and discrimination; b. provide services to victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination; c. fulfill the special needs of women; and

d. improve family quality.

Article 10

Prevention of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women is implemented in an integrated and coordinated manner coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

Article 40

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered, with its placement in the Regional Gazette of Kebumen Regency.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 28

(1) Regional Government in an effort to provide and implement protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation and violence establishes UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and responsible to the head of the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and children's protection.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, principal tasks and functions as well as management of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizers of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to be able to carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officials which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the energy or abilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 33. Discrimination as intended is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children experiencing violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group, hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK, is a community-based women and children protection institution that is based and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to residence.

Article 29

(1) Regional Government conducts coordination in handling protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation, and discrimination at the sub-district level by establishing a women and children protection forum.

(2) Membership of the women and children protection forum as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of Sub-district, Sector Police, Military District Command, Public Health Center, Office of Religious Affairs and other elements.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by respect for human rights is respect for, upholding the human rights inherent in citizens, and protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Letter b

What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or actions for vulnerable women's groups with the aim that they obtain equality of rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c

What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that depicts equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, and in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by usefulness is the organization of protection for women that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Subparagraph f

Sufficiently clear.

Subparagraph g

What is meant by victim-based decisions is that decision-making regarding services provided must be based on approval/confirmation with the victim.

Subparagraph h

Sufficiently clear.

Subparagraph j

Subparagraph k

What is meant by sustainability is services to women victims carried out thoroughly and completely in accordance with the needs of victims and have interconnections between one form of service and another form of service.

Verse (2)

Sufficiently clear.

Verse (3)

Sufficiently clear.

Article 27

Subparagraph a Sufficiently clear. Subparagraph b Sufficiently clear. Subparagraph c Sufficiently clear. Subparagraph d What is meant by other women's protection and empowerment institutions are institutions or organizations that provide services, counseling, consultation, provision or dissemination of information, outreach and empowerment for families proportionally, including referring targets to other service institutions needed by families whose establishment is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 22

What is meant by related agencies are agencies that have a role in implementing women's empowerment in the social sector, including women and child protection institutions, legal aid organizations and victim of violence assistance, safe houses (shelters) that handle gender-based violence victims, psychology practitioners and counselors, universities/educational institutions, community organizations, Family Welfare Empowerment, gender study centers at universities, family counseling consultation institutions, religious organizations that have women's empowerment programs, social rehabilitation centers.

Article 34

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage up to the policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women for the current year.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by respect for human rights is respect for, upholding the human rights inherent in citizens, and protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Letter b

What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or actions for vulnerable women's groups with the aim that they obtain equality of rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c

What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that depicts equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, and in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by usefulness is the organization of protection for women that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizers of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officials which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the energy or abilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 33. Discrimination as intended is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group, hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK, is a community-based women and children protection institution that is based and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to residence.

Article 26

Regional Government is responsible for:

b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women; and

Article 13

(1) The fulfillment of special needs of women relates to the protection of women from all things that may threaten the safety and/or health of women's reproductive organs.

(2) The fulfillment of special needs as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:

a. health services, especially family planning services, pregnancy, childbirth, post-childbirth, breastfeeding and menstruation;
b. fulfillment of the right to obtain paid leave including maternity leave; and
c. provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women.

Article 34

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage up to the policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women for the current year.

Article 35

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus organizing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment periodically.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 10

Prevention of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women is implemented in an integrated and coordinated manner coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizers of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to be able to carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officials which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the energy or abilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 33. Discrimination as intended is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children experiencing violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group, hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK, is a community-based women and children protection institution that is based and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to residence.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

Article 34

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage up to the policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women for the current year.

Article 28

(1) Regional Government in an effort to provide and implement protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation and violence establishes UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and responsible to the head of the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and children's protection.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, principal tasks and functions as well as management of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN PROTECTION EFFORTS

Article 35

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus organizing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment periodically.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for organizing the protection and empowerment of women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities.

Article 26

Regional Government is responsible for:

a. implementing policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in order to realize the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women; and
c. applying service standards for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in physical, sexual, and psychological suffering or misery to women, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of persons not to experience discrimination, suffering or misery either directly or indirectly committed by state officials or by the state or by regional government officials or individuals which constitute natural rights granted by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which includes complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizers of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to be able to carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officials which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the energy or abilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 33. Discrimination as intended is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA, is an operational technical implementation unit within a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children experiencing violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group, hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK, is a community-based women and children protection institution that is based and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to residence.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

(1) Regional Government in an effort to provide and implement protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation and violence establishes UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and responsible to the head of the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and children's protection.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, principal tasks and functions as well as management of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT Article 25

Obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:

a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women conducted by the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Integrated Service is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the organizers of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to be able to carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officials which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or to the family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the energy or abilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 33. Discrimination as intended is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of the recognition, implementation or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group, hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK, is a community-based women and children protection institution that is based and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to residence.

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in governmental affairs which are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can self-regulate and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of diminishing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, and obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in suffering or misery physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in physical, sexual, and psychological suffering or misery to women, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of persons not to experience discrimination, suffering or misery either directly or indirectly committed by state officials or by the state or by regional government officials or individuals which constitute natural rights granted by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which includes complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can self-regulate and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of diminishing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Violence is any action that results in suffering or misery physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in physical, sexual, and psychological suffering or misery to women, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of persons not to experience discrimination, suffering or misery either directly or indirectly committed by state officials or by the state or by regional government officials or individuals which constitute natural rights granted by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which includes complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

Article 8

The implementation of women's protection includes efforts to: a. prevent violence, exploitation, and discrimination; b. provide services to victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination; c. fulfill the special needs of women; and

d. improve family quality.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(2) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business sector and other related stakeholders.

Obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:

Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including actions: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is entirely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any action that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an action that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering in a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence expressly referred to as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in statutory provisions. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, persons who have family relationships by blood, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent to a woman or group of persons not to experience discrimination, suffering or misery either directly or indirectly committed by state officials or by the state or by regional government officials or individuals which constitute natural rights granted by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which includes complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 8

d. improve family quality.

CHAPTER V

Obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:

a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for victim handling to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women conducted by the Regional Apparatus that conducts governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 33

(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the organization of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) The participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the authorized agency if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

b. conducting prevention actions against violence towards women; and

c. conducting skills training.

CONCERNING

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women constitute an inseparable part of citizens who possess human rights that must be safeguarded and fulfilled without exception. However, various issues such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is also still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that sides with vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, and enhance the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.
